company.name: Pennine Refreshment Services Ltd
company.description: Independent operated vending and unattended retail route operator running cold drink, snack, fresh-food and bean-to-cup hot drink machines across Greater Manchester, the M62 corridor, Leeds, Sheffield and Liverpool from a depot and ambient/chilled warehouse at Trafford Park, Manchester. Services around 640 placed machines and micromarkets in factories, distribution centres, NHS sites, universities, leisure centres and transport hubs on fixed route-and-frequency schedules, with route drivers restocking from on-van stock against each machine's planogram, collecting cash and coin from coin mechanisms and note recyclers, reconciling takings to telemetry-reported audit sales, and rotating chilled and fresh-food stock under date control. Operates a mixed 3.5t box/chiller van and panel van fleet plus a 7.2t refrigerated rigid for warehouse-to-route transfers, holding a standard national goods vehicle operator (O) licence with the North West of England Traffic Area Office of the Traffic Commissioner for its operating centre at Trafford Park. Vending telemetry (Nayax/Televend DEX cashless and audit data) drives demand-based route planning, machine fault alerts and cash reconciliation. Statutory DVSA MOT, tachograph downloads on the 7.2t rigid, FSA-registered food business chilled-chain and HACCP temperature monitoring, and odometer/engine-hour preventive maintenance are managed in FleetFlow. Restock confirmations, cash bag seal numbers, machine planograms and fridge temperature logs are captured per visit.

metadata.generatedNote: Operating-week summary, 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-28. The business runs fixed route-and-frequency schedules per machine: route drivers fill to each machine's planogram from on-van stock, empty coin mechanisms and note recyclers, seal cash bags and reconcile takings to the Nayax/Televend DEX audit within a 2% variance threshold. Chilled and fresh-food lines are rotated first-in-first-out under use-by date control; short-dated stock is pulled and waste logged. The chilled chain is held from warehouse to van to machine with a temperature log per visit (HACCP, FSA-registered food business). The 7.2t refrigerated rigid runs warehouse-to-route transfers and micromarket deliveries under EU 561/2006 drivers' hours with a digital tachograph, on the operating centre's goods vehicle operator (O) licence. Statutory DVSA MOT class 7, tail-lift LOLER thorough examinations, NHS Government Buying Standards healthy-vending planograms, and odometer/engine-hour preventive maintenance apply. Currency GBP.

workOrders.notes: Twice-weekly restock round (Mondays and Thursdays) for the nine machines at Trafford Park Logistics. Fill all banks to planogram from on-van stock R01, rotate fresh-food and chilled by use-by date and pull anything short-dated. Collect coin from the four paid machines and reconcile takings to the Nayax DEX audit. Hot-drink and free-vend machines need ingredient top-up and a wipe-down. Report to the gatehouse on arrival.

Weekly Wednesday restock at Bramwell Engineering. Hot-drink machine is set to free-vend for the shop floor - top up beans, topping and cups and descale check. Fill the snack and cold-drink machines to planogram and collect coin from the paid units. Ear protection required on the shop floor.

Tuesday/Friday restock across the University of Sheffield estate - machines in the Students' Union, Information Commons and libraries. Mostly cashless so card volumes are high; still empty the note recyclers and coin on the paid units and reconcile to DEX. Bean-to-cup needs descale and milk-system clean. Top up fast-moving energy drinks and meal-deal snacks.

Micromarket and machine replenishment at Mersey Leisure aquatics centre. Restock the open chilled fridge and grab-and-go wall to planogram, rotate by use-by, record fridge temperature and pull short-dated sandwiches and protein pots. Self-checkout kiosk is cashless but the adjacent drink machine takes coin - collect and reconcile. Chilled chain must be maintained from van to fridge.

Weekly warehouse-to-route transfer on the 7.2t DAF - bulk chilled and ambient cages from Trafford Park warehouse out to the Interchange and DC machine banks for the high-volume routes, plus cups and coffee ingredient pallets. Tacho applies (over 3.5t). Maintain chilled chain; record body temperature throughout.

High-footfall daily top-up at the Metrolink Interchange concourse. Cashless-only machines so no coin to collect - priority is keeping fast movers in stock through the commuter peaks. Demand-led using DEX sell-through; fresh-food grab-and-go rotated by date. Saturday visit included; closed Sundays.

Three-times-weekly restock across the 18 machines at Northern General Hospital - concourse and ward floors. Healthy-vending planogram applies under Government Buying Standards for Food, minimum 70% healthier lines; fresh-food rotated tightly by date. Lift access to wards. Collect coin and notes, reconcile to DEX and report monthly commission. ID badge required.

Scheduled planogram reset on the Information Commons snack machine - delete three slow lines, bring in the summer range, convert two spirals for larger sharing bags and update pricing in the controller. Relabel lanes and reflash the planogram from the back office.

Telemetry-raised callout - the fresh-food machine on the NGH concourse has tripped its health-control lockout with cabinet temperature above 8C, so vending is inhibited as designed (food safety). Engineer to diagnose the refrigeration, check the condenser and fan, and dispose of any stock that has been out of temperature. Priority because it is a fresh-food unit in a hospital.

New bean-to-cup install at the Mersey Leisure gym reception. Deliver and position on the 7.2t with tail-lift, plumb into the mains water and power, fit a Nayax cashless reader, set the planogram and pricing and commission with a test-vend. Customer to confirm the water and power point before delivery.

Quarterly cash reconciliation completed for the Bramwell machines. Coin counted in the depot coin room came to GBP1,842.60 against a DEX expected total of GBP1,851 - a -0.45% variance, well within the 2% threshold, so no investigation needed. Variance put down to a couple of free-vend overrides and a known sticky coin acceptor on the snack unit, which the engineer has since cleaned.

Fill all banks to planogram from on-van stock R01, rotate fresh-food and chilled by use-by date and pull anything short-dated. Collect coin from the four paid machines and reconcile takings to the Nayax DEX audit. Hot-drink and free-vend machines need ingredient top-up and a wipe-down. Report to the gatehouse on arrival.

Weekly Wednesday restock at Bramwell Engineering. Hot-drink machine is set to free-vend for the shop floor - top up beans, topping and cups and descale check. Fill the snack and cold-drink machines to planogram and collect coin from the paid units. Ear protection required on the shop floor.

Tuesday/Friday restock across the University of Sheffield estate - machines in the Students' Union, Information Commons and libraries. Mostly cashless so card volumes are high; still empty the note recyclers and coin on the paid units and reconcile to DEX. Bean-to-cup needs descale and milk-system clean. Top up fast-moving energy drinks and meal-deal snacks.

Micromarket and machine replenishment at Mersey Leisure aquatics centre. Restock the open chilled fridge and grab-and-go wall to planogram, rotate by use-by, record fridge temperature and pull short-dated sandwiches and protein pots. Self-checkout kiosk is cashless but the adjacent drink machine takes coin - collect and reconcile. Chilled chain must be maintained from van to fridge.

Weekly warehouse-to-route transfer on the 7.2t DAF - bulk chilled and ambient cages from Trafford Park warehouse out to the Interchange and DC machine banks for the high-volume routes, plus cups and coffee ingredient pallets. Tacho applies (over 3.5t). Maintain chilled chain; record body temperature throughout.

High-footfall daily top-up at the Metrolink Interchange concourse. Cashless-only machines so no coin to collect - priority is keeping fast movers in stock through the commuter peaks. Demand-led using DEX sell-through; fresh-food grab-and-go rotated by date. Saturday visit included; closed Sundays.

Three-times-weekly restock across the 18 machines at Northern General Hospital - concourse and ward floors. Healthy-vending planogram applies under Government Buying Standards for Food, minimum 70% healthier lines; fresh-food rotated tightly by date. Lift access to wards. Collect coin and notes, reconcile to DEX and report monthly commission. ID badge required.

Scheduled planogram reset on the Information Commons snack machine - delete three slow lines, bring in the summer range, convert two spirals for larger sharing bags and update pricing in the controller. Relabel lanes and reflash the planogram from the back office.

Telemetry-raised callout - the fresh-food machine on the NGH concourse has tripped its health-control lockout with cabinet temperature above 8C, so vending is inhibited as designed (food safety). Engineer to diagnose the refrigeration, check the condenser and fan, and dispose of any stock that has been out of temperature. Priority because it is a fresh-food unit in a hospital.

stops.notes: Picked the Trafford Park round from the warehouse pick list, loaded 8 chilled and 14 ambient totes plus cup and ingredient boxes. Van fridge pre-chilled to 4C before chilled stock loaded. Coin float of GBP60 signed out.

Filled all nine machines to planogram from on-van stock - 612 units across snack, drink, fresh-food and bean-to-cup. Rotated fresh-food and chilled by date and pulled 11 short-dated sandwiches and yoghurts. Fresh-food cabinet temp 5C, within range.

Collected coin from the four paid machines - GBP318.40 counted against a DEX expected GBP322.10, -1.15% variance (within threshold). Sealed into bag SEAL-771204 and logged. Cashless sales come straight off Nayax.

Returned to depot, dropped the sealed coin bag in the coin-room safe and logged it. Returned 11 short-dated chilled items for write-off. Van plugged into shore power overnight to keep the fridge cold.
Loaded the NGH round - heavier chilled load for the healthy fresh-food planogram. Healthier snack and drink lines picked to meet the 70% ratio. Coin float GBP80 signed out for two cash machines.

Restocked all 18 machines across the concourse and four ward floors - 1,184 units. Healthy ratio held at 72%, above the 70% Government Buying Standards minimum. Pulled 22 short-dated fresh-food items. One concourse snack lane jammed and was cleared.

Collected coin and notes from the six cash-accepting machines - GBP441.70 coin and GBP120 notes against DEX expected GBP569.50, -1.36% variance. Sealed bag SEAL-771210. Note recyclers on the concourse units emptied.

Loaded the Sheffield University round - heavy on energy drinks and meal-deal snacks for the cashless-heavy estate. Coffee beans and topping for the bean-to-cup. Coin float GBP40 for the few coin acceptors.

Serviced all 14 machines across the SU, Information Commons and libraries - 936 units. Bean-to-cup descaled and milk system cleaned. Energy-drink lanes were nearly empty on arrival - bumped facings per the DEX sell-through data.
Mostly cashless campus - cash take only GBP166.30 (coin GBP96.30 plus GBP70 notes) against DEX GBP168.20, -0.89% variance. Cashless was 84% of sales. Note recyclers emptied. Bag SEAL-771221.

Replenished the micromarket open fridge and grab-and-go wall - 408 units, rotated by date, pulled 9 short-dated sandwiches and protein pots. Open-fridge temperature 4C, recorded in the HACCP log. Faced up the shelving and tidied the self-checkout area. Completion photos uploaded.
Self-checkout micromarket is cashless; only the adjacent protein/isotonic drink machine takes coin - GBP74.20 collected against DEX GBP75. Bag SEAL-771233.

Loaded the 7.2t for the bulk route transfer - 6 chilled and 10 ambient cages plus cup and ingredient pallets. Body pre-cooled to 3C before chilled cages loaded. Tail-lift and walkaround check passed; tacho card inserted.
Dropped 3 chilled and 5 ambient cages to the Trafford Park site store for the local machine banks. Body temperature 4C on delivery, signed for by the site store.
Delivered the remaining 3 chilled and 5 ambient cages plus cup pallets to the Interchange concession store ready for the daily top-ups. Body 4C, signed for. Returned empty cages to depot.

Daily fast-mover top-up across the 12 cashless Interchange machines before the morning commuter peak - 524 units, focusing on energy drinks, water and meal-deal sandwiches per the DEX sell-through. No cash to collect (cashless-only). Fresh-food cabinet 5C.
Loaded the Bramwell weekly round - snacks, cold drinks, coffee beans, topping and cups for the free-vend hot-drink machine. Small coin float for the two paid units.

Restocked the five Bramwell machines - 386 units. Topped up beans, topping and cups on the free-vend hot-drink machine and confirmed it is still set to no-charge for the shop floor. Ear protection worn on the floor. Coin collected from the two paid units.
Collected coin from the snack and cold-drink machines - GBP132.80 against DEX GBP134.50. Bag SEAL-771248. Free-vend hot-drink machine has no cash.

Found the fresh-food machine's condenser coil clogged with dust, causing the cabinet to overheat and trip the health-control lockout. Cleaned the condenser, checked the fan and refrigerant pressures, ran it back down to 4C and reset the health control. Quarantined 18 units that had been out of temperature for disposal; logged on the food-safety record.
Planned: pick and load the Trafford Park round (visit 48) - chilled and ambient totes per pick list, pre-chill the van fridge, sign out coin float.
Planned restock of the nine Trafford Park machines to planogram, fresh-food date rotation, coin collection and DEX reconciliation.
In progress - 11 of 18 machines filled so far, concourse done and three of four ward floors. Healthy ratio holding at 71%. One ward floor and the cash collection still to do.

Quarterly cash audit - counted coin from all five machines for the quarter and compared to DEX. GBP1,842.60 counted vs GBP1,851 expected, -0.45%, within threshold. Found a sticky coin acceptor on the snack machine; engineer cleaned it the same day.

Deep clean - stripped and sanitised the fresh-food drum cabinet and full descale plus milk-system clean on the bean-to-cup. HACCP cleaning log updated. Machines refilled and back in service. Completion photos uploaded.
Visit 121 daily top-up at the Interchange - 498 fast-mover units before the peak. Cashless-only, no cash. Two drink lanes had sold out overnight; refaced to planogram.
Planned Friday Sheffield University restock - 14 machines across three buildings, bean-to-cup descale due, coin and note collection and DEX reconciliation.
Loaded the 7.2t for the Interchange transfer - 4 chilled and 8 ambient cages. Body pre-cooled to 3C, tail-lift checked, tacho card in. Departing for the concourse drop.
In transit / unloading at the Interchange concession store - delivering 4 chilled and 8 ambient cages for the daily top-ups. Body temperature 4C.
Returned from NGH, dropped the sealed coin and note bag in the coin room and logged it. Returned 22 short-dated fresh-food items for write-off. Van on shore power overnight.
Returned from Liverpool, dropped sealed bag SEAL-771233 in the coin room, returned 9 short-dated chilled items for write-off and put the van on shore power.

payload.desc: diesel particulate filter efficiency below threshold - soot accumulation

payload.note: machine refrigeration alert recorded against the servicing route vehicle (R04)

payload.reason: DPF fault and sliding door runner

notes.author: Workshop - Fleet Engineer
notes.body: R06 came in with a DPF efficiency fault (P2002) on Geotab - soot load reading 96%. It's been doing short stop-start route work and never getting a chance to regen. VOR'd it, ran a forced regeneration on the diagnostic tool, and while it's off the road I'm sorting the nearside sliding door runner that's been catching. Aiming to have it back for Saturday. Relief route covered by R01 and R04 doubling up where needed.

notes.author: Tomasz Kowalski (DRV-306)
notes.body: NGH fresh-food machine callout sorted. The cabinet had tripped its health-control lockout - temperature was reading 9.4C, well over the 8C limit, so the machine had correctly stopped vending for food safety. Root cause was the condenser coil packed with dust killing the refrigeration. Cleaned the condenser, checked the fan and refrigerant pressures, pulled it back down to 4C and reset the health control. Had to quarantine 18 units that had been out of temperature for disposal - logged on the food-safety record. Recommended this unit goes on a more frequent condenser-clean schedule.

notes.author: Priya Sharma (DRV-304)
notes.body: NGH three-times-weekly restock done. All 18 machines filled, concourse and four ward floors - 1,184 units. Held the healthy ratio at 72%, above the 70% Government Buying Standards minimum, so we're compliant on the healthy-vending planogram. Pulled 22 short-dated fresh-food items. One concourse snack lane had jammed on a sharing bag that was too wide - cleared it and noted that line for a spiral conversion.

notes.author: Yard Foreman
notes.body: R01 column tail-lift LOLER thorough examination is due 18 August - last one was February. Booking it in with the lift company in good time. Fridge unit was serviced in May and is holding temperature fine; the body logger has been reading a steady 4 to 5C on the chilled side all week, well within the 8C alarm.

notes.author: Transport Manager
notes.body: Susan's driving licence expires 30 September while she's on leave. Sent her the DVLA renewal link. She's our main relief route driver so I need this sorted before she's back covering rounds. Her food hygiene and cash-handling tickets are all fine. Flagged on the compliance board.

notes.author: Mark Whitaker (DRV-301)
notes.body: Trafford Park cash collection done. Coin from the four paid machines came to GBP318.40 against a DEX expected GBP322.10 - that's -1.15%, within our 2% threshold. The small shortfall is the usual: a couple of test vends and the odd coin returned. Sealed into bag SEAL-771204 and logged. Cashless on these is climbing - more than half of sales now go through the Nayax readers.

notes.author: Darren Sutcliffe (DRV-303)
notes.body: Sheffield Uni round done - all 14 machines across the SU, IC and libraries, 936 units. The energy-drink lanes were nearly empty on arrival so I bumped the facings on the back of the DEX sell-through; they're flying through exam resits. Descaled the bean-to-cup and cleaned the milk system. Campus is heavily cashless now - 84% of sales on card this visit - but I still emptied the note recyclers and coin.

notes.author: Operations
notes.body: The chilled body logger on the 7.2t is doing exactly what we need - read 3.4C at load, drifted to 4.1C by the second drop, never near the 5C alarm. We're keeping these temperature logs against every transfer run for the FSA chilled-chain records. The Carrier unit was serviced end of May.

notes.author: Account Manager
notes.body: TfGM concession team still hasn't signed off the new summer salad and wrap range for the Interchange grab-and-go (WO-3012). Chased the concessions officer again. It's on hold anyway while R06 is in the workshop limiting our spare cover, but I'd like it live before the school holidays footfall picks up. The current range is selling through fine in the meantime per DEX.

notes.author: Cash Office
notes.body: Q2 cash reconciliation for Bramwell closed. Counted GBP1,842.60 in the coin room against a DEX expected GBP1,851 - a -0.45% variance, comfortably within the 2% threshold so no investigation. We did find a sticky coin acceptor on the snack machine VM-BRAM-02 that was occasionally rejecting good coins; engineer cleaned and tested it the same day. Free-vend overrides on the hot-drink machine account for the rest of the gap.

notes.author: Mark Whitaker (DRV-301)
notes.body: Interchange daily top-up done before the peak - 524 units into the 12 cashless machines. Energy drinks, water and the meal-deal sandwiches are the fast movers here; pulled the DEX sell-through on the way over and weighted the load to suit. Two drink lanes had emptied overnight - refilled to planogram. Fresh-food cabinet at 5C, all good. No cash on this site, all card.

notes.author: Yard Foreman
notes.body: R01 due its 78k service - currently on 74,210, so about 3,800 miles out, roughly three to four weeks at current mileage. MOT is fine until March. Will book the service in for mid-July when the route diary allows - Susan can cover Route A in the relief van if needed, once her licence is renewed.

notes.author: Priya Sharma (DRV-304)
notes.body: Trafford Park deep clean completed last week - stripped and sanitised the fresh-food drum cabinet and did a full descale and milk-system clean on the bean-to-cup. Both back in service the same shift, HACCP cleaning log updated and signed off by Helen the facilities manager. The drum cabinet seals are starting to perish - flagged for replacement at the next visit.

notes.author: Priya Sharma (DRV-304)
notes.body: NGH restock - heavy on chilled today. Loaded the van fridge first thing pre-chilled to 4C and it held all run. Filled the fresh-food drum, faced up the healthier snack and drink lines to keep the 70% ratio, rotated everything by date. Pulled 22 short-dated items. Lift to the ward floors was busy with beds so it took longer than usual on the upper floors.
